sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that receiving influence from a level above the chain of descent requires self-nullification, as illustrated by the distinction between the Sefirah of Chessed called "Gedulah" in the world of Tohu and "Chessed" in Atzilus, and how the attribute of "Chessed Zuta" specifically comes about through lowliness and bittul, enabling the revelation of the higher "Gedulah."

translations.translation: Now, this is also the case regarding influence from above,
that in order to receive the influence of a level that is above the chain of descent, it is specifically through bittul (self-nullification).
And as explained by the Rebbe Maharash58
on the verse59
"Who is a G-d like You, bearing iniquity and passing over transgression for the remnant of His heritage," and our sages said,60
"For one who makes himself like remnants,"
for at first glance it is not understood,
for is not forgiveness drawn from a very high place, which is above the place of exacting judgment, and why specifically for one who makes himself like remnants?
And he explains this with an introduction61
regarding what the early Kabbalists before the Ari z"l called the attribute of Chessed by the name "Gedulah," and the Ari z"l called the attribute of Chessed by the name "Chessed."
And the reason for this is,
because the early Kabbalists spoke about the matter of the Sefiros of Tohu,
and the Chessed of Tohu is in the aspect of Gedulah, unlike the Ari z"l who speaks about the aspect of Chessed of Atzilus, and therefore he calls it simply Chessed.
And this Chessed
(Chessed of Atzilus)
is also called by the name "Chessed Zuta" (the Small Chessed).
And the reason that this Chessed is called by the name Chessed Zuta,
is not that the Chessed itself is small, for the influence of this Chessed is also in abundant measure,
as it is brought in the book Orchos Tzadikim62
regarding Avraham Avinu
(who was a chariot for the Chessed of Atzilus63)
that he was generous with his money, his body, and his soul.
And what it is called by the name Chessed Zuta is not because the Chessed itself is small, but rather because the Chessed comes about through the cause of smallness (katnus),
meaning that the influence of the Chessed of Atzilus is due to bittul.
And so too Avraham
(who was a chariot for the Chessed of Atzilus as mentioned above),
for because he was lowly in his own eyes, as it says64
"And I am dust and ashes,"
therefore he would bestow all good and kindness upon others.
And this is also the matter of "I am unworthy of all the kindnesses"65
that Yaakov said,
as explained in Igeres HaKodesh.66
Now, although the Chessed of Atzilus is called simply Chessed or Chessed Zuta, and the title Gedulah applies to the Chessed that is above the chain of descent,
nevertheless, it is explained in many places in the interpretation of the verse67
"Yours, Hashem, is the greatness (Gedulah) and the might (Gevurah) etc." that it refers to the Sefiros of Atzilus.
And he explains this,
that because Chessed Zuta comes about through the aspect of smallness (katnus),
that one makes himself small and lowly until he is considered as nothing,
therefore, for this very reason, it is a vessel to receive the influence of the aspect of Chessed that is above the chain of descent, which is called Gedulah,
and on the contrary,
the revelation of the aspect of Gedulah is specifically within the aspect of Chessed Zuta.
And this is "Who is a G-d like You... for the remnant of His heritage," for one who makes himself like remnants,
that the drawing down of the aspect of the revelation of the Ein Sof light that is above the chain of descent is specifically to one who makes himself like remnants,
the aspect of bittul to the ultimate degree.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section distinguishes between the bittul of Chochmah (the bittul of "Ayin") and the bittul of Kesser (the bittul of "Effes"), explaining that the bittul drawn into Binah is only from the external aspect of Chochmah, while the internal aspect of Chochmah and the bittul of Kesser represent higher levels of nullification, culminating in the bittul of silence.

translations.translation: Now, although it was explained above in section 4
(in the explanation of this maamar)
that the matter of bittul
(meaning essential bittul)
is specifically from the aspect of Chochmah,
nevertheless, through the revelation of the illumination of Chochmah within Binah,
the bittul of Chochmah is drawn also into Binah.

However, the aspect of Chochmah that is revealed in Binah is only the aspect of the externality of Chochmah that is related to Binah, unlike the aspect of the internality of Chochmah, which is above the aspect of the source for Binah.
And as explained by the Rebbe
(the Rebbe Rashab)
of blessed memory, in the Hemshech of 5666,68
that in the letter Yud
(which alludes to Chochmah)
there are two matters.
The first is the letter Yud with its filling of Vav-Dalet, which is the aspect of the externality of Chochmah that is related to Binah,
and the second is the letter Yud itself without the filling, which is the aspect of the essence of Chochmah that is not in the aspect of a source for Binah.
And one can explain this based on what is stated in the Siddur69
and in the discourse on the Miluyim (fillings),70
that the matter of the filling is for the sake of another.
For when one needs to say the letter Yud in speech to another, then the letters Vav-Dalet are necessarily added,
unlike as it is in thought, where it is only a single letter
(the Yud itself).
Based on this, it is understood,
that the letter Yud with its filling of Vav-Dalet is the aspect of the externality of Chochmah that is related to Binah
(for Binah is like "another" relative to Chochmah),
unlike the letter Yud itself without the filling, which is the aspect of the essence of Chochmah.
And these two aspects within Chochmah are also distinct in the aspect of the bittul within them,
as is understood from what is explained in the Hemshech of 5666 there,
that the aspect of the externality of Chochmah is analogous to the aspect of light
(the aspect of water)
that spreads and becomes invested in vessels,
and the aspect of the internality of Chochmah is analogous to the aspect of light that is above the matter of investment in vessels.
Now, even the bittul of the aspect of the internality of Chochmah is not in the aspect of the utter absence of existence.
For even Chochmah is in the aspect of a "color" (gaven), only that its color is an essential color.
And as explained in that Hemshech, that the bittul of Chochmah is the bittul of "Ein Od Milevado" (there is nothing besides Him),
the meaning of "Ein Od Milevado" is that there is no existence apart from the Essence (Atzmus), but together with the Essence there is existence,
and this bittul is the bittul of light
(as it is in the aspect of revelation)
which has no existence of its own apart from the luminary (HaMaor),
but together with the luminary it is in the aspect of existence.
For this bittul is specifically in the aspect of light that spreads,
unlike the bittul of the light that is included within the luminary, which is the bittul of "Effes" (naught/cessation)
(which is above the bittul of "Ayin")
and it is that even with Him, blessed be He, there is no existence at all.
For this bittul is in the aspect of the light when it is included in the luminary, and all the more so in the aspect of "Yashet Choshech Sistro" (He made darkness His hiding place),71
which is the aspect of darkness and concealment that is above the aspect of light
(even above the aspect of included light).
And this is the difference between the bittul of the aspect of Chochmah and the bittul of the aspect of Kesser,
that the bittul of Chochmah is the bittul of the aspect of "Ayin" (nothingness),
unlike the bittul of Kesser, which is the bittul of the aspect of "Effes" (naught/cessation),
for this is what Kesser is, from the term "Kesser Li Z'eir" (a little while I will be silent),72
which is the matter of silence,
for the bittul of silence is above even the bittul of the internality of Chochmah.
And this is what they said,73
"Silence is a fence for wisdom,"
for these three words allude to the three aforementioned aspects.
"Fence" (Sig) alludes to the bittul of the externality of Kesser,
for this is that "Sig" in gematria equals "Chochmah,"
meaning it is above the bittul of the aspect of Chochmah itself, and only the gematria
(and the concealment of Chochmah)
alone.
"Wisdom" (Chochmah) is the bittul of the aspect of Chochmah itself.
And "Silence" (Shtikah) is the bittul of Kesser,
and as mentioned above, that Kesser is from the term "Kesser Li Z'eir," which is the matter of silence.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the previous concepts to the Zoharic statement "Every Rav is from Bavel, every Rabbi is from Eretz Yisrael," explaining that the letter Yud added in "Rabbi" according to the Baal Shem Tov's interpretation represents a level above the Yud with its filling, which is the essence of Chochmah itself.

translations.translation: And one can connect this with the statement of the Tikkunim,74
"Every Rav is from Bavel, every Rabbi is from Eretz Yisrael,"
and it is explained in Shaar Maamarei Rashbi,75
that when He, blessed be He, goes forth to the outside,
to the diaspora
(Bavel),
He does not go forth from the aspect of the Names (Havayos), but rather comes in the aspect of the three fillings of Ayin-Bet, Samech-Gimel, Mem-Heh.
And this is what is said,76
"Behold, Hashem rides upon an Ayin-Bet Kal (a swift cloud),"
the explanation,
for He does not go forth to the diaspora except in the aspect of Ayin-Bet Kal
[which is the filling of the Name of Mem-Heh (45) with Alephs, as is known],
and behold, Ayin-Bet Kal in gematria is Resh-Bet (202),
and therefore every Rav is from Bavel.
But in Eretz Yisrael,
then he is called Rabbi,
because there the ten letters of the Name Havayah are combined with their filling, which is Ayin-Bet Kal,
and it all equals in gematria Reish-Beis-Yud (Rabbi)
(end of quote).
And the Baal Shem Tov adds77
in his interpretation of the statement "Every Rav is from Bavel and every Rabbi is from Eretz Yisrael,"
that "Rav" (Resh-Beis) refers to the aspect of Chochmah and Binah,
"Reish" is the beginning of wisdom (Chochmah), "Beis" is the aspect of Binah,
and the letter Yud that is added in "Rabbi" is the flow from the Ein Sof.

And one can say that the aspect of the Yud that is added in "Rabbi" according to the Baal Shem Tov's explanation is above the aspect of the Yud mentioned above according to the explanation in Shaar Maamarei Rashbi.
For according to the explanation in Shaar Maamarei Rashbi, the Yud is the ten letters
[which is the Yud with its filling,
only that it is elevated more than the aspect of the filling that is in gematria Ayin-Bet Kal],
unlike according to the Baal Shem Tov's explanation, it is the Yud itself, which is above the aspect of filling.
